newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's NSW coal miners call strike.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's NSW coal miners call strike.

text.p: Coal miners in the Australian state of New South Wales will strike from 1200 GMT (11.00 p.m.) on Thursday over a 25 percent cut in accident compensation payouts, a union official said.
The coal miners' union estimates the strike will cost the industry A$12.5 million a day.

"It will effect about 12,000 coal miners in New South Wales and obviously have a significant impact on the waterfront as coal shipments will cease to be moved, and that's a tragedy," said John Maitland, national president of the Construction, Foresty, Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU).
"And it is just unfortunate you end up with one of these confrontations which will do damage to our reputation and it's all about pig-headedness," Maitland said in a statement.
The upper house of the New South Wales parliament voted late on Wednesday to include coal miners in plans to cut lump sum compensation payments for seriously injured workers.
The Labor government, which controls the lower house but not the upper house, originally excluded coal miners from the cuts.
The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and CRA-RTZ have significant coal mining operations in the Hunter Valley region in central New South Wales.
